newsitem.title: CANADA: Investors watch new Bema discovery.
newsitem.headline: Investors watch new Bema discovery.

text.p: Trading in Bema Gold Corp was busy on Tuesday after the company said it had made another major gold discovery in Chile.
Shares in the Vancouver-based gold mining and exploration company rose C$0.60 to C$11.15 by mid-afternoon, in heavy trading of 1.3 million shares.

Drilling on Bema's Quebrada property has outlined new mineralization in a zone the company calls Quebrada Seca. Bema reported six drill holes late Monday, four of which intersected high-grade mineralization, the company said. Analysts warned that drilling is still in the early stages.

"There's obviously a lot of mineralization in the system," company chairman and chief executive officer Clive Johnson said in a phone interview. "It's very early, but we feel very comfortable that we're on to a big discovery here."
Results so far suggest the company has found a gold porphyry deposit which could contain a higher grade zone, he said.
Bema is also working to expand Refugio production in the next few years, Johnson said. The Refugio mine is north of the newly discovered Quebrada Seca area.

At the company's Cerro Casale find on the nearby Aldebaran property, Bema expects to have a new resource calculation in late April or early May and a pre-feasibility study by the end of the year, Johnson said.
He estimates the deposit contains at least 15 million ounces. Bema may consider bringing in a partner to bring Cerro Casale into production, he added.
Bema owns 49 percent of the Aldebaran property. Arizona Star Resource Corp owns the other 51 percent. Bema owns 30 percent of Arizona Star.
Bema owns 100 percent of the Quebrada property and 50 percent of the Refugio mine.
